Land purchase in Judea and Samaria
Israelis, including Jews, should be allowed to buy land in Judea and Samaria (the West Bank) freely, even if this deepens Israel's hold on the territory.
Torah study, civilian service or conscientious objection should count as legitimate alternatives to military service, even if fewer people serve in the army.

The right to equality should be written into Israel's Basic Laws, including the Nation-State Law, even if this gives the courts more grounds to strike down laws.
Party lists and public bodies should be required to include a fair share of women, even if parties lose some freedom to choose their candidates.
The working week should be shortened by law, for example to four and a half days, even if the economy produces less.

Unemployment benefits should be extended to the self-employed, medical interns and people in vocational training, even if National Insurance spends more.
Students and pupils should get more state support, such as study grants, free school meals and tuition aid, even if this costs the budget more.
Gun licensing should be stricter and illegal weapons fought harder, even if fewer citizens can carry a gun for self-defense.
Citizens should have more ways to challenge government and police decisions in court and through appeals, even if the authorities find it harder to act quickly.

Teachers, lecturers and public employees who express support for terrorism should be dismissed, even without a criminal conviction.
The state should open more universities and colleges, including in the north and in Arab towns, and ease admission rules such as the psychometric exam, even if academic standards may fall.
Israel should withhold tax money it collects for the Palestinian Authority to offset payments to terrorists and their families, even if the Authority's finances collapse.
The state should give more funding and tax breaks to charities and non-profits, such as organizations for disabled veterans and food donations, even if it collects less tax.

Widows, widowers, orphans and bereaved families should get more benefits, for example equal survivors' pensions for widowers, even if this costs the budget more.
The state should give farmers more support, such as cheaper water and investment grants, even if taxpayers and consumers pay more.
Soldiers and police should have immunity from prosecution for actions during operations, even if some abuses go unpunished.
Voting should be made easier — for aircrews, students and citizens serving abroad — and never conditioned on military or national service, even if elections cost more to run.

Patients should get more legal rights, such as treatment within a set time and a ban on conversion therapy for minors, even if health providers bear higher costs.
смешанное: внутри законопроекты о хамеце в больницах
Municipalities should get more powers, for example to run public transport on Shabbat, set up local guard units and approve building plans, even if rules differ from town to town.
Cameras should be installed in daycare centers and special education and used to record police crowd-control actions, even if this intrudes on staff privacy.
More people should qualify for disability, nursing-care and sick-leave benefits, for example homemakers and the self-employed, even if National Insurance spends more.
The state should impose stricter environmental rules, such as a climate law, a levy on plastic bags and protection of trees and coasts, even if this raises costs for businesses and consumers.
Reservists, people with disabilities and other residents should get bigger discounts on municipal property tax and parking, even if local councils have less money.
Debtors should be better protected — for example no electricity cut-offs for unpaid bills and no travel bans over small debts — even if creditors find it harder to collect.

The army, police and intelligence services should face more external oversight, including a state commission of inquiry into October 7, even if this exposes political and military leaders to criticism.

Cannabis should be legal for personal use, even if drug use may increase.
Tax enforcement should be tightened, for example by limiting cash payments and collecting VAT at source in construction, even if businesses face more paperwork.
People under a protective order for domestic violence should be electronically monitored, even before any conviction.
Old-age pensions and allowances for Holocaust survivors should be raised and means tests removed, even if this costs the budget more.
The state should expand free public education, from early childhood to after-school programs and learning-disability diagnosis, even if this requires more spending.
Animal protection laws should be tightened, for example by banning trawling, poisons and animals in entertainment, even if farmers, fishers and businesses bear costs.
The prime minister should be limited to two consecutive terms and Supreme Court justices to a fixed term, even if voters lose the option to re-elect a popular leader.
